transcription.tex: \text{\textbf{Turning points}\quad How does the degree restrict the shape?}
\text{A polynomial of degree n has \textbf{at most} n−1 turning points. It can have fewer: \(y=x^4\) has just one.}
\text{\textbf{End behaviour}\quad What determines the direction of the tails?}
\text{The leading term dominates for large \(|x|\). For example, if \(y=ax^2+bx+c\) and \(a>0\), then \(y\to\infty\) as \(x\to\pm\infty\).}
\text{An upward quartic need not have three turns. Do not infer the number of turns just from its degree.}
